title: High-Performance Thermo-Acoustic Blankets over the Aft Cargo Compartment Ceiling
abstract: Replacement of the standard insulation over the aft cargo ceiling by a two-layer blanket with a limp mass barrier, launched to cut airborne sound transmission into the rear cabin on a targeted group of high-density aircraft.

sections.reason: A group of operators running high-density layouts on the oldest airframes score consistently worst on rear-cabin comfort surveys, and the dominant path measured during a two-aircraft survey campaign was airborne transmission through the aft cargo ceiling rather than through the fuselage sidewall. The insulation over that ceiling is the original thermal standard, chosen for heat rather than for sound, and it has compacted after twenty years so that its thickness is now roughly two-thirds of the as-built value. The eight aircraft named in this modification are the ones where the survey was flown and where the operators have committed to a cabin refresh.
sections.description: The existing insulation over the aft cargo compartment ceiling is replaced by a two-layer blanket comprising a lofted thermal layer and a limp mass barrier laminated to its inner face. The lining latch D2550114658909 is renewed because the thicker blanket changes the panel standoff, the lighting kit D2550118482429 is re-positioned on a deeper bracket, and the restraint decor panel D2550136675057 is re-profiled at the ceiling junction. Blind rivets LN181986-9B secure the new blanket retainers to the monument fitting D2550007584379. The cargo lining light FIN 3596DQ and the latch FIN 76DL are relocated by 40 millimetres and the compartment panel FIN 6DL is unchanged. Work is done from inside the aft cargo compartment in zones 131, 134, 143 and 146 with the ceiling lining panels removed. Drawings D25500026668 issue H and D25500014455 issue A carry the blanket layout and the retainer positions.
sections.effects: Estimated mass increase of 34 kg per aircraft, aft of the centre of gravity, giving a shift of about 0.14 per cent MAC. No electrical load change at the aircraft level. The blanket is interchangeable with the original insulation as a maintenance item, but the deeper standoff brackets are not, so a compartment must be converted in full. Predicted reduction in rear-cabin sound level is 3.5 dB(A) at cruise. The blanket must be re-qualified against the compartment flammability and the smoke penetration requirements, and the cargo compartment ventilation path has to be re-checked because the ceiling clearance falls by 22 millimetres.
sections.open_points: The second round of pre-analysis must settle whether the reduced ceiling clearance affects the smoke detection sampling flow, whether the cargo lighting retrofit already embodied on part of this group forces a different bracket, and whether an earlier cancelled proposal for the same compartment left any released drawing content that has to be withdrawn.

type_data.balance_impact: Aft mass addition, CG shift approximately 0.14 % MAC
type_data.production_impact: No production cut-in; the current build standard already carries an acoustic blanket in this position
